sources.title: Nashik District Government: History, Rashtrakuta dynasty
sources.note: Directly read. Restricted use of the named Wani grant of 808 and Dantidurga/Krishna succession; several other dates and legendary statements on this general page are unreliable and unused.

sources.title: Lisa N. Owen: The multireligious caves at Ellora
sources.note: Art historian original essay, 2021. Indexed full relevant sections read; direct fetch failed. Trenches and coordinated carving in Kailasanatha section; smaller Jain adaptation in final section.

sources.title: UNESCO: Ellora Caves
sources.note: Original institutional description and outstanding universal value read. Different cave groups span periods before and after the imperial dynasty; never assign the whole site to one ruler.

sources.title: British Library, WD2216(62): Kailasanatha temple drawing
sources.note: Indexed original catalogue read. Identifies the temple with Krishna I and Mount Kailasa; the catalogue item is a later drawing, not itself an eighth-century object.

sources.title: F. Kielhorn and H. Krishna Sastri: Salotgi pillar inscriptions, Epigraphia Indica IV, pages 57 to 66
sources.note: Original ASI edition, 1896 to 1897, mirrored OCR directly read and checked against downloaded scan. Inscription A records a September 945 donation, engraved subsequently. Text page 60 line 1 visually verified; translation pages 62 to 63. B and C are separate records; C is later and not used. Dwellings are not explicitly twenty-seven student dormitories.

sources.title: D. C. Sircar: Rashtrakuta Charters from Chinchani, Epigraphia Indica XXXII, pages 45 to 60
sources.note: Original ASI epigraphic edition directly read via mirror. First charter, Saka 848 / 926 CE; discussion page 52, verses 16 to 23 and prose lines 27 onward. Free ferries on two streams, rice/curries/ghee, Arab governor and village endowment. The later grants in this volume are not treated as the same document.

sources.title: J. J. O’Connor and E. F. Robertson: Mahavira, MacTutor, University of St Andrews
sources.note: Directly read scholarly mathematics biography. Text around 850, chapter list, place-value numerals, operations and combinatorics. Avoid absolute first-in-world claims and mistaken division-by-zero rule.

sources.title: Yashwant K. Malaiya, Colorado State University: Mahaviracharya
sources.note: Directly read university faculty historical note. Connects the 850 mathematical treatise to Amoghavarsha and quotes the introduction on practical applications.

proposedOverrides.name: Rashtrakuta Empire
proposedOverrides.summary: A major Deccan empire remembered for literature, learning and rock-cut temples.

batchIdentityNotes.historicalScope: Imperial Rashtrakutas of the eighth to tenth centuries, not every earlier or later family using the name.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Decoded world-800: [72.759,11.254,79.062,20.514]; world-900: [72.759,11.254,84.901,23.001]. Broad Deccan outlines, not exact jurisdiction or campaign limits; political collapse around 973 publicly distinguished from imported 1000 endpoint.
batchIdentityNotes.sourceLimits: No medical or household toilet reconstruction found in the selected evidence. Food, ferries, school finance, craft and mathematics are specific supported everyday examples.
